title: Rava son of Rav Ada
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He and Ravin son of Rav Ada (possibly his brother, in Hyman’s conjecture) were students of Rav Yehudah, as in Beitzah 33b, where they said, “When we were at Rav Yehudah’s.”
Both spoke in Rav Yehudah’s name, as in Taanit 24b and Ketubot 7b. Both spoke in Rabbah’s name, as in Yoma 53b.

We likewise find “Rabbah son of Rav Ada said that Rav said,” as in Kiddushin 70a, and “Rabbah son of Rav Ada said that Rav Ada said that Rav said,” as in Menachot 39a; Hyman suggests that possibly in Yoma and Kiddushin too the words “Rav Ada” are missing in the middle. In Makkot 18a: “Rava bar Ada said that Rabbi Yitzchak said”; in Sukkah 3a: “Rabbah son of Rav Ada said: It is needed only,” etc.
Hyman reports that in the Venice printing it was written רב׳, and from this came Rabbah; but in fact his name was Rava.

notes.text: Possible brotherhood and the omitted Rav Ada are Hyman’s conjectures. His Venice-apostrophe explanation is reported, not new printed-pixel or correction-history evidence.
